submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) at 30 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency of 93.292% at the allocated 8 kHz rate. This is significantly better than Algorithm-L2 (best: 86.624% at 35 GeV) and Algorithm-L3 (best: 74.009% at 40 GeV). The 30 GeV threshold was found to be optimal for Algorithm-L1 through systematic exploration of the 20-60 GeV range, with efficiency peaking at this value. All candidate algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget and optical link bandwidth constraints, making Algorithm-L1 the superior choice for maximizing signal efficiency.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 at 30 GeV achieves 93.292% signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate, which is the highest among all tested configurations across all three candidate algorithms.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) is listed as one of the three candidate algorithms in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: All candidate algorithms, including Algorithm-L1, fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs) and the 25 Gb/s optical links have enough bandwidth for all candidate algorithms.
The recommended threshold of 30 GeV is within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.
